channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Passenger Dies in Bishkek E-Bike Accident, Driver Arrested
item.description: A passenger on an electric bicycle died after being hit by a car in Bishkek on September 27. The driver of the Mazda 323, suspected of being intoxicated, was detained. A criminal case has been initiated.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Participates in CSTO Military Exercises in Russia
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is participating in the CSTO military exercises 'Interaction-2026', 'Search-2026', and 'Echelon-2026' held at the Chebarkulsky training ground in Russia. The exercises involve contingents from Kyrgyzstan, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Russia, and Tajikistan.

item.title: Central Asian customs agencies to enhance data exchange and risk management
item.description: Customs authorities from Kazakhstan, China, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan agreed on a draft procedure for operational data exchange. The document, to be signed at the 3rd China-Central Asia summit in 2027, aims to accelerate cargo movement, improve customs control accuracy, and increase trade route transparency. Discussions also covered AI and big data in customs risk management.

item.title: Kazakhstan's exports to Turkey surge, driven by coal and engines
item.description: Kazakhstan's trade with Turkey reached $4.7 billion in January-July 2026, a 1.6-fold increase. Exports grew significantly in coal, oil products, and copper. While exports of polymers and cotton fiber decreased, imports also declined, notably in clothing and confectionery.

item.title: Iran ready for 'apocalyptic war' if provoked, says Foreign Minister
item.description: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that while he and President Masoud Pezeshkian came to New York with a message of peace, Iran is prepared for an 'apocalyptic war' if provoked. He reiterated Iran's steadfastness against any aggression and readiness for 'real diplomacy'.

item.title: Tajikistan inaugurates new solar, wind, and hydro power facilities in Gorno-Badakhshan
item.description: President Emomali Rahmon commissioned new energy facilities in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Province on September 27. These include a 110/35 kV substation in Ishkashim, a 3 MW solar power station in Shughnan, a 112 kW solar station in Rushan, and a 25 kW small hydropower plant in Bartang.

item.title: US-Iran indirect talks resume today with Qatari mediation, media reports
item.description: A new round of indirect negotiations between the United States and Iran is scheduled to take place today, according to Axios, citing sources. Mediators from Qatar will hold separate meetings with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff.

item.title: China ready to work with all nations for historical multilateralism and shared development
item.description: China is prepared to collaborate with all countries to preserve historical multilateralism and promote global development initiatives, ensuring benefits for all. Chinese Vice President Han Zheng stated this at a UN meeting, emphasizing that these initiatives address the needs of the Global South and have transitioned from concepts to international actions.

item.title: Serbian President Resigns, Paving Way for Early Elections
item.description: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić has resigned, opening the path for early presidential elections. He will not run again, having served two terms. Parliament Speaker Ana Brnabić will assume presidential duties temporarily. Vučić may seek the prime minister position.

item.title: Uzbekistan's representative addresses UN General Assembly, highlighting regional cooperation
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration of Uzbekistan, spoke at the 81st UN General Assembly session. Her address focused on openness, dialogue, and cooperation, presenting Uzbekistan's stance on international security, UN reform, regional issues, Afghanistan, ecology, AI, and human capital. The speech emphasized the new dynamics in Central Asia and Uzbekistan's active role in shaping the regional agenda.

item.title: Uzbekistan Chess Team Wins 46th World Chess Olympiad
item.description: The Uzbekistan national chess team has achieved a historic victory at the 46th World Chess Olympiad. The team, comprising talented players and coaches, secured the title of two-time Olympiad champions. They demonstrated exceptional intellect, willpower, skill, and courage against strong international competition.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tops World Kickboxing Championship in Italy
item.description: The Kazakhstan national kickboxing team secured first place in the overall medal standings at the World Kickboxing Championship for juniors and youth in Lido di Jesolo, Italy. Kazakh kickboxers won a total of 66 medals, including 25 gold, 20 silver, and 21 bronze, across various disciplines and age categories.

item.title: Turkmenistan awards military personnel with high state honors and new military ranks
item.description: In recognition of their contributions to national defense and maintaining law and order, and marking the 35th anniversary of Independence, Turkmenistan's President Serdar Berdimuhamedow has signed decrees awarding military and law enforcement personnel with special ranks and professional qualifications. These honors recognize exemplary service and significant achievements in strengthening the nation's defense capabilities and ensuring public order.

item.title: US and Russia Remove Key Clause on Autonomous Weapons from Draft Agreement
item.description: The United States and Russia have removed a significant clause concerning autonomous weapons from a draft agreement. Negotiations for the agreement, which could have set rules for the use of lethal autonomous weapons, took place in early September at the UN in Switzerland.

item.title: Uruzgan residents report stalled construction of Aghajan Dam two years after groundbreaking
item.description: Residents of Uruzgan province state that construction of the Aghajan Dam, promised to irrigate over 100,000 hectares, has not begun two years after its groundbreaking ceremony. The dam was intended to have a storage capacity of over 70 million cubic meters. Local residents express concern over worsening drought conditions and the impact on their livelihoods.

item.title: Uzbekistan's tourism sector sees significant growth, with foreign tourist numbers increasing sixfold
item.description: Uzbekistan's tourism sector is experiencing significant growth, contributing to job creation and economic well-being. The country has seen a sixfold increase in foreign tourists since 2016, reaching nearly 12 million in 2025. Tourism service exports grew elevenfold to $4.8 billion. Uzbekistan was recognized as one of the world's fastest-growing tourist destinations.

item.title: Afghan citizens report increasing Taliban restrictions on religious freedom and ceremonies
item.description: Afghan citizens are reporting growing restrictions on religious freedom since the Taliban's takeover, affecting the observance of ceremonies and rites. Followers of Shia, Ismaili, and Sunni faiths are calling for respect for religious freedom, emphasizing that it includes the free performance of religious activities. They warn that continued restrictions could harm interfaith coexistence and religious diversity.

item.title: Freedom Front Claims 37 Taliban Killed, 24 Wounded in Nuristan and Kunar Clashes
item.description: The Afghanistan Freedom Front (AFF) announced that 37 Taliban fighters were killed and 24 wounded during clashes in Kamdesh district of Nuristan and Nari district of Kunar. The AFF stated that its forces counterattacked after the Taliban attacked their positions, recapturing several villages and capturing Taliban outposts and weapons.

item.title: Pakistan Denies Taliban Claims of Involvement in Nuristan Conflict
item.description: Pakistan's Ministry of Information and Broadcasting has rejected the Taliban's claims of Pakistani involvement in recent clashes in Afghanistan's Nuristan province, calling them "baseless and devoid of truth." The ministry stated that no evidence was provided and that videos supporting the claim showed unarmed individuals in a staged scenario.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Life Imprisonment for Sexual Violence Against Children
item.description: Shahnoza Mirziyoyeva, First Deputy Director of the Agency for Social Protection, announced that proposals to increase penalties for child sexual abuse, including life imprisonment for perpetrators of sexual violence against children, have been submitted to relevant authorities.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Role in Initiating the C5+1 Diplomatic Platform
item.description: Kazakhstan played a key role in the creation of the C5+1 diplomatic format, which engages the United States with Central Asian nations. The platform, established in 2015, has evolved beyond foreign minister meetings to include presidential summits and cooperation on trade, security, and energy. Kairat Umarov, Kazakhstan's ambassador to Washington, is credited with initiating the process.

item.title: US and Iran May Hold New Round of Indirect Talks on September 28, Media Reports
item.description: The United States and Iran may conduct a new round of indirect negotiations on September 28, according to Axios, citing two regional sources. President Trump also indicated he expects continued contact with Tehran this week. Qatar continues to mediate the discussions, which previously took place in New York.

item.title: Afghanistan's central bank and ACGF sign agreement to boost financial sector
item.description: Da Afghanistan Bank (DAB) and the Afghan Credit Guarantee Foundation (ACGF) signed a memorandum of understanding to strengthen the financial sector and expand access to finance for businesses. The agreement includes technical support and grants totaling approximately $1 million for small and medium-sized businesses in the first phase.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber Launches Investigation into Ministry of Defense
item.description: Kazakhstan's Supreme Audit Chamber has initiated a state audit of the Ministry of Defense, focusing on the effective use of budget funds and material-technical support. The audit follows a presidential order for a comprehensive review of the ministry's operations, prompted by recent incidents and a focus on digital transformation.

item.title: Kazakh President Warns Military After Caspian Tragedy, Demands Reform
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has tasked the Defense Ministry with improving budget efficiency and reforming the armed forces. Following the deaths of 14 servicemen during Caspian exercises, he stressed that accountability for mismanagement and theft will be enforced. Transparent criteria for personnel selection based on competence, not loyalty, are also required.

item.title: Kazakh President Acknowledges Failures in Military After Caspian Incident
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev criticized the military's lack of responsibility and professionalism following a deadly Caspian exercise. He noted inadequate equipment and poor coordination, stating the army is stuck in the past. The president warned that all responsible officers, regardless of rank, will face legal consequences.

item.title: Kazakhstan to deploy drones for labor safety monitoring
item.description: Kazakhstan is introducing aerial monitoring, drones, and intelligent video analytics into its state labor inspection work. New technologies aim to strengthen labor safety oversight at industrial enterprises. Drones will monitor high-altitude facilities, while video analytics will detect violations in real-time, according to Egemen.kz.

item.title: Tokayev demands army command system overhaul after deadly drills
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has called for a fundamental transformation of the army's command system, stating it is 'stuck in the last century.' The demand follows the deaths of 14 servicemen during naval exercises in the Mangystau region due to adverse weather conditions. Tokayev emphasized the need for digital transformation and replacing human roles with technology where possible.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders Defense Ministry Probe After Fatal Exercise
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a comprehensive review of the Ministry of Defense following a fatal military exercise. He noted that servicemen lacked essential equipment, including life vests. A government commission will assess officials' actions and identify those responsible for the shortcomings.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Blames 'Criminal Unprofessionalism' for Soldier Deaths
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has attributed the deaths of 14 servicemen during exercises in the Mangystau region to the "criminal unprofessionalism" of officers, including generals. He stated that irresponsibility, negligence, and showing off have become commonplace, undermining the country's defense capability. An investigation into the Ministry of Defense's work has been launched.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Highlights Lack of Equipment for Servicemen
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that servicemen participating in exercises in the Mangystau region were not adequately equipped, lacking essential gear like special life vests. He emphasized the need to ensure personnel safety and announced a comprehensive inspection of the Ministry of Defense's operations, including equipment and financial provisions.

item.title: UN Meeting: Taliban Learned Crossing Red Lines Has No Cost, Says Special Rapporteur
item.description: At a UN General Assembly sideline meeting, speakers urged an inclusive Afghan political process, respect for human rights, and accountability for the Taliban. The Special Rapporteur stated the Taliban have learned they can cross international red lines without consequence, advocating for unified international pressure.

item.title: Tokayev: Those who embezzle budget funds will not escape responsibility
item.description: President Tokayev stated that individuals who embezzle budget funds will be held accountable. He emphasized that allocated finances must enhance the country's defense capabilities and yield maximum results, with no tolerance for aimless spending or embezzlement.

item.title: President Tokayev tasks Defense Minister with strengthening ideology and education work
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev instructed the Defense Minister to enhance ideology and education within the armed forces, emphasizing effective budget spending, military reform based on modern threats, and merit-based personnel selection. The goal is to foster professionalism and patriotism.

item.title: Tokayev blames criminal unprofessionalism for deaths of 14 servicemen
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev stated that the deaths of 14 servicemen during exercises in Aktau were due to the criminal unprofessionalism of officers. He assured that ranks and positions would not exempt anyone from responsibility and that the matter is under his personal control.

item.title: WHO reports 170 deaths from respiratory illnesses in Afghanistan
item.description: The World Health Organization (WHO) announced 170 deaths from acute respiratory illnesses in Afghanistan, with 64,506 cases reported. The number of cases decreased by 17.4% compared to July. The WHO also reported 1,423 suspected measles cases and seven deaths, a decrease from July.

item.title: Kazakh President Criticizes Military Officers for Negligence After Fatal Incident
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev strongly criticized military officers, including generals, for negligence and unprofessionalism following the deaths of 14 servicemen in the Mangystau region. He pledged full support to the families of the deceased and demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances and planning of the training exercise.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Undertake Military Reform with Clear Action Plan
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a military reform in Kazakhstan, emphasizing the need for a concrete, phased plan to address modern threats. The plan, to be developed by the Security Council apparatus and the Ministry of Defense, will focus on transparent personnel selection based on competence, not loyalty, and efficient budget utilization.

item.title: Tajikistan reaffirms support for peace and stability in Afghanistan
item.description: Tajikistan reiterated its support for the Afghan people, emphasizing that peace, stability, and economic opportunities in Afghanistan are crucial for regional security. Foreign Minister Sirodjiddin Muhriddin stated that lasting security and development depend on the situation in Afghanistan.

item.title: Tokayev Orders Military Reform After 14 Soldiers Die in Training Exercise
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered a comprehensive reform of the armed forces following the deaths of 14 servicemen during a training exercise. He criticized the military's outdated equipment and lack of professionalism, stating that accountability will be established for those responsible for the tragedy.
